architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created reusable admin detail components (DetailsCard, DetailsValue) for consistent presentation of key-value data across admin panels
architecture_decisions.rationale: The admin panel needed consistent styling for displaying team/organization details. Creating reusable components ensures design consistency, reduces code duplication, and makes future maintenance easier. The components support features like monospace fonts, selectable text, and action buttons.
alternatives_considered: Creating separate components for each detail type

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created a shared global settings display component that handles both team and organization settings with inheritance logic
architecture_decisions.rationale: Global settings exist at both team and organization levels with inheritance relationships. The AdminGlobalSettingsSection component handles parsing email settings, displaying inherited values, and showing appropriate labels for both contexts. This avoids duplicating complex rendering logic across multiple pages.
alternatives_considered: Separate components for team vs organization settings

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added a new tRPC endpoint for fetching team details with comprehensive related data
architecture_decisions.rationale: The team details page requires data from multiple related tables (team, organization, members, invites, settings). Creating a dedicated endpoint with proper typing ensures type safety, reduces client-side data fetching complexity, and allows for optimized database queries with includes.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Enhanced navigation between related admin pages with clickable links and improved data relationships
architecture_decisions.rationale: Admin users need to navigate between related entities (organizations → teams → users). Adding clickable links to team names, showing IDs for reference, and providing clear navigation buttons improves usability and workflow efficiency.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Enhanced organization member tables to show roles, IDs, and team relationships with proper role hierarchy resolution
architecture_decisions.rationale: Organization members can have different roles across multiple teams. Using getHighestOrganisationRoleInGroup and getHighestTeamRoleInGroup utilities ensures the displayed role reflects the member's highest privilege level. Showing user IDs and creation dates provides audit trail information.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive error handling and loading states for the new team details page
architecture_decisions.rationale: The team details page needs to handle invalid IDs, missing teams, and loading states gracefully. Using the existing GenericErrorLayout pattern ensures consistent error presentation across the admin panel.

implementation_summary:
The implementation enhances the admin panel with improved organization and team management capabilities through a systematic approach. First, reusable UI components (DetailsCard, DetailsValue, AdminGlobalSettingsSection) were created to ensure consistency across new and existing admin pages. These components handle the presentation of key-value data, global settings with inheritance logic, and proper internationalization.

A new team details page was implemented at `/admin/teams/$id` that displays comprehensive team information including identifiers, relationships, global settings, members with their roles, and pending organization invites. The page integrates with a new tRPC endpoint (`admin.team.get`) that fetches related data from multiple tables in an optimized query, ensuring type safety through Zod schemas.

The existing organization page was enhanced to show usage metrics (members and teams against limits) and display global settings in a collapsible accordion. Navigation between related entities was improved by making team names clickable in tables, showing user and team IDs for reference, and adding clear navigation buttons between organization and team pages.

Key patterns used include: consistent error handling with GenericErrorLayout, proper role hierarchy resolution using existing utility functions, copy-to-clipboard functionality for IDs, and maintaining the existing design system. The changes integrate seamlessly with the existing codebase by following established patterns for admin routes, tRPC procedures, and component organization.
